rationale.headline: Brazil are favoured to beat Japan, winning roughly 46 times out of 100 to Japan's 29.

drivers.label: Chance-creation form
drivers.detail: Across the group stage Brazil created 1.3 more good chances per game than they gave up, versus 0.6 for Japan — Brazil simply made better chances more often.

drivers.label: Earned standing, not lucky results
drivers.detail: Brazil are rated on how convincingly they out-created opponents, not on tight scorelines, so wins built on real dominance count more than results that hinged on a single lucky goal.

drivers.label: Margin of safety
drivers.detail: The gap is wide enough that Japan would need a clear upset to advance.

rationale.methodNote: Market-blind: each team's pre-tournament Elo prior is replayed through the group stage using expected-goal difference as the match outcome — a logistic merit score S_xG = 1/(1+e^(-1.8·xGD)) drives a standard Elo update (scale 400, K=24) so chance-creation, not the raw scoreline, moves ratings; the fixture is then converted to 1X2 via a Davidson ties model on the neutral-venue rating difference. Inputs are FIFA on-pitch xG and Elo priors only — no betting or prediction-market data was used.
